original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-affine}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\{X_i \to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-fpqc-covering}.
Let $(V_i/X_i, \varphi_{ij})$ be a descent datum
relative to $\{X_i \to S\}$. If each morphism
$V_i \to X_i$ is quasi-affine, then the descent datum is
effective.

final_content.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal U=\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ a family of morphisms, and $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ a descent datum for schemes relative to $\mathcal U$: each $X_i$ is an $S_i$-scheme, and $\varphi_{ij}:X_i\times_S S_j\overset{\sim}{\to} S_i\times_S X_j$ is an isomorphism over $S_i\times_S S_j$, satisfying the usual cocycle condition on triple overlaps. Such a datum is *effective* if it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum $(S_i\times_S X,\mathrm{can})$ arising from some $S$-scheme $X$. Assume $\mathcal U$ is an fpqc covering and each $X_i\to S_i$ is quasi-affine, meaning that locally on the base the source is quasi-compact and an open subscheme of an affine scheme over that base. Then the descent datum $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ is effective. In particular, the relative affine hulls $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{S_i}((p_i)_*\mathcal O_{X_i})$ descend by affine descent, and the compatible quasi-compact open subschemes $X_i$ descend to an open subscheme of the resulting affine hull over $S$.
hypotheses: fpqc cover and a scheme descent datum whose local structure maps are quasi-affine.

semantic_review_note: Pinned descent.tex L9232 assumes a scheme-valued descent datum over an fpqc cover and all V_i→X_i are QUASI-AFFINE. The proposal uses the standard relative characterization by quasi-compact open embeddings into relative affine hulls, descends the hulls and opens, and concludes effectiveness, without wrongly demanding that each V_i be affine.
